subject: Proposal: Hosted API commit uplift + harmonized rate bands for Velaris Renewal
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Kovacs <elena.kovacs@velaris-retail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Hosted API commit uplift + harmonized rate bands for Velaris Renewal

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time on Tuesday. As we discussed, Q4 traffic for Velaris typically doubles year-over-year and we want to be sure your storefront experience stays snappy while keeping per-token costs predictable. Attached is a short proposal (spreadsheet) that outlines a couple of commit uplift options and a harmonized rate band approach that reduces surprise overage charges during promotional spikes.

Quick summary: 
- Option A: 2.5M token / month commit (12-month) — 18% discount vs current list, smoothing window for seasonal spikes
- Option B: 4.0M token / month commit (12-month) — 24% discount + 10% burst capacity available with pre-approved throttling policy

Would you be available for a 30-minute sync next week to pick an option and agree start date? If you prefer, I can route a single amendment (clean) to procurement for signature once you confirm the choice.

I CC'd Laura to align on finance/discounting constraints.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: Velaris_commit_proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42kb)

From: Elena Kovacs <elena.kovacs@velaris-retail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@velaris-retail.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Hosted API commit uplift + harmonized rate bands for Velaris Renewal

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear options. Two quick clarifying Qs before we lock a meeting:
1) For Option B, can you summarize how the burst capacity is billed when it triggers? (flat overage rate or tiered?)
2) Do we get an SLO on median latency at the 95th percentile once we move to the higher commit? Our legal team flagged the need to avoid regression on current tail latency.

Procurement here is curious about the amendment timeline too — if we confirm by end of week can you guarantee a start date of Oct 1?

Thanks —
Elena
Head of Engineering, Velaris Retail
---
(Procurement looped in: procurement@velaris-retail.com)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Kovacs <elena.kovacs@velaris-retail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Hosted API commit uplift + harmonized rate bands for Velaris Renewal

Elena —

Thanks — quick answers inline: 
1) Burst billing: we use a tiered overage band for bursts. For Option B the first 10% over the monthly commit is billed at the Option B overage rate (which is lower than current list), then standard overage beyond that. We can include a cap (soft cap + notification) and automatic throttling policy that will pause non-critical requests if burst consumption exceeds the safety threshold for >10 minutes.
2) Latency SLO: Yes — for the 4.0M commit we can guarantee a 95th percentile median latency target for typical storefront prompt sizes (under 1.2s P95). We’ll include that in the amendment and add a rollback/fallback to a smaller-context model if the SLO is breached.

If that looks correct, Option B is our recommended path for peak Q4 traffic. I attached a draft amendment (redline-ready) — legal can use that to prepare the DocuSign.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm Option B by EOD Wed 8/19
- I route amendment + pricing appendix to procurement and legal
- Target effective date Oct 1, 2026 (billing starts on first invoice)

Laura/Ben/Karthik — can we confirm the 24% discount and the burst cap language? Ben I think finance flagged a minimum 12-month term for that band; happy to sync if you need more detail.

Best,
Jordan
---
Attachment: Velaris_AMENDMENT_draft_v1.pdf (PDF, 68kb)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Hosted API commit uplift + harmonized rate bands for Velaris Renewal

Jordan / team —

18% for Option A is fine; for the recommended Option B I can sign off on 24% discount for a 12-month commitment provided procurement accepts the burst throttling cap and we include the standard annual true-up language. Put legal on notice to prepare an amendment with those two bullets: (1) 24% discount on list price for 4.0M token monthly commit, (2) 10% burst band billed at reduced overage then throttle policy kicks in, (3) P95 latency SLO as submitted.

Laura — please confirm billing cadence and whether finance needs any additional PO language.

Ben
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

> > Elena —
> > (answers and proposed next steps)

From: Elena Kovacs <elena.kovacs@velaris-retail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@velaris-retail.com, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Hosted API commit uplift + harmonized rate bands for Velaris Renewal

Thanks everyone — this all looks acceptable from our side. Procurement will sign the amendment once the DocuSign is available. A couple of final asks: 

- Please include a single paragraph in the amendment that calls out the performance fallback (model variant) we discussed.
- Can you confirm the invoice cadence and whether billing will be monthly in arrears or prepaid for the first month? We prefer monthly in arrears but can be flexible if needed.

We are prepared to execute Option B (4.0M / month, 12 months) contingent on the final amendment language and DocuSign link. Target start date Oct 1 works for us.

Elena
Head of Engineering, Velaris Retail
